answer.diagnosis: No shortcut found: every trained unit reads the blob's radial size profile, and I found no off-centre, label-specific patch. The trained layer-1 units come in two mirrored families. (1) Ring units (2, 4, 14, 17, 18, 19, 25, 26, 29, 30) have a positive centre near (11.5, 11.5), a strongly negative annulus at radius about 4-6, and positive weights farther out. They detect small blobs and feed layer-2 unit u11, which carries a negative output weight. (2) Disc units (3, 7, 8, 21, 22, 24, 27, 28) are roughly the sign-flip of the ring units, with a positive annulus at radius about 4-7 that only a large blob covers. They detect large blobs and feed u0, u1, u5, u7 and u8, which carry positive output weights. The remaining units (0, 1, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 20, 23, 31) have small, uniform-looking weights of about ±25. They look like untrained initialisation and encode nothing structured. I looked for a localised, contiguous, one-sided feature, such as a corner square, a border stripe, a marker dot or a bar, that is consistently signed across the trained units and comparable in strength to the size template. I found none. The corners, the border and a candidate bar on row 9 hold only noise-level values. The background does contain some isolated spike pixels, for example (8,2), (3,12), (1,17) and (20,19) favouring small, and (0,11), (23,11) and (0,4) favouring large. These sit on both sides with roughly symmetric heavy tails, and mostly lie near radius 10-12, where the radial template already has its outer ring. They look like noise in one shared template rather than a spurious cue. Their agreement across units is expected, because all trained units are near-copies of that one template. The decision therefore appears to rest on blob size, so I make no edits.
